_about: Content map for the reading-library project (see PROJECT_STATUS.md). One entry per source document in cefr/texts/. Drives conversion to reading/{level}/{slug}.html + assets/audio/reading/{level}/{slug}.mp3. Authored from a full read of all 98 extracted source documents, not from filenames.

_fields.words: word count of the .docx-extracted source (docx preferred over pdf per instruction)
_fields.genre: reading | dialogue | drill | discussion | reference — drills/discussions are not reading texts, so audio is n/a
_fields.level: recommended CEFR level after audit (the source library was flat/unlevelled)
_fields.action: KEEP | EDIT | MERGE | SPLIT | RECLASSIFY | CONVERT | REPLACE | DELETE
_fields.status: NOT STARTED | AUDITING | EDITED | CONVERTED | IMPLEMENTED | REVIEWED | COMPLETE

_audio_note: 19 mp3 files already exist in cefr/texts for 6 texts (attention-economy, capetown, cars, hiking-in-the-mountains, physical-education, snowy-days). Where the audit calls for editing that text, the existing audio becomes stale and MUST be regenerated (requirement 8.6).

texts.reason: Pure simple-past gap-fill on accounting tasks; no prose passage. Becomes a fill-blank block.
Two concatenated A1 review sheets, 2036w. Split into themed A1 review blocks.
Well-formed A2 mixed-grammar drill set; converts cleanly to fill-blank/multiple-choice.
Strong, genuinely C1 essay on the founding. Dense academic register; trim and break into sections for readability.
Three unrelated things in one file: a culture overview, a corndog/state-fair food piece, and passive-voice grammar drills. Split into a B2 culture reading, a B1 food reading, and a drill block.
Reads as marketing copy for a named vendor (Gallagher), not a teaching text. Replace with a neutral do/make farm-work reading.
Excellent airport-arrival functional dialogue. Traveler renamed to an English name; trim repetition in the shuttle exchange.
Clean, well-pitched C1 argument text. Already has 3 mp3 segments.
Bulleted travel-tips list, not connected prose. Rewrite the Sydney half as a short A2 reading; drop or fold the Thailand half.
Factual slip: 'Pilsner: Pilsen is a type of lager'. Fix, tighten the style list.
Useful tech-history angle but list-like and abrupt; convert to connected prose.
Sound process text. Slug de-accented for safe hosting; retitle from the odd 'Distilled Spirit Visitation'.

Clear, well-levelled text on income and car choice. Has 4 mp3 segments.
Good vocabulary load; over-casual asides ('this beast drives the whole operation') to even out.
Text points at images that do not survive conversion ('Here is a chilling traditional image of Krampus'). Rewrite those references out.

Word-bank gap-fill; its answer key is a separate file to fold in.

Whole text written in the past tense for a simple-past drill, which makes it factually wrong: 'Cybersecurity protected computers...', 'Today, we used the internet'. Rewrite in present tense and move the past-tense practice to a separate drill.
Identical '_____ (to verb) ___ (in/on/at)' template to navigating-finance and unfortunate-events; three copies of one exercise.

do/make contrast is forced into unnatural English ('Do the feeding of the cattle'). Rewrite with collocations people actually use.
Good present/past A2 narrative. Relocate to a US setting and use an English name, per the project's American-context brief.
Presents a UFO sighting as documented history and invites the student to research it 'as a doctoral student'. Misinformation framed as scholarship; replace with a real Thutmose III / Karnak reading.
The legitimate Egypt text; keep as the single Egypt reading and trim.
Dated to a specific forecast year and written for one Brazilian city ('what does it mean for someone who lives in porto alegre'). Stale and off-brief; nothing here is worth migrating.

The register contrast is worth teaching, but the informal sample argues developing nations are poor because 'they suck at running their countries'. Keep the formal/informal exercise shape, replace the topic with a neutral one.
Technical word-bank gap-fill; answer key is a separate file.
Answer key for formula-1.
Natural, well-levelled travel-trend text.
Idioms crammed in at an unnatural density, one of them crude for a classroom ('crews have busted their butts'). Keep the present-perfect focus, rewrite the register.
Multiple-choice-in-brackets dialogue drill; maps directly to fill-blank with options.
A writing worksheet whose body is blank rules for handwriting. Becomes guided writing prompts, not a reading.

Blog-register news brief with an emoji mid-text, and graphic content (gang rape, torture, starvation) unsuitable for a general adult English class. Replace with a current-affairs reading that teaches the same analytical language.
Simple, natural past-tense narrative. Has 2 mp3 segments.
Long question-formation drill across several tenses; split by tense into separate blocks.
Tight interrogation dialogue, natural past continuous, English names already.

Annotated restaurant list for Milan — no connected prose, no American context. Replace with a US dining-out reading.
Passives exist only to demo the form and read badly ('The tickets were bought by her', 'I gave a big hug to her'). Rewrite naturally.
Third copy of the same gap-fill template as daily-activities and unfortunate-events.
